summary: The registry stores each live task.notification (from live-task-notifications) in the SQLite message mirror as a user row whose content is taskNotificationText(event), id storedTaskNoticeId(threadId, taskId) = tasknotice_<thread>:<task id>, INSERT OR IGNORE and stamped with the event's own time, so it is stored once per task. The CLI queues some notices and removes them without writing a transcript line; those used to vanish on reload. On load-session-by-id, mergeConversationMessages pairs a stored notice with a transcript <task-notification> part of the same task id (nearest in time), else one without a task id whose status and summary match within 5s; a paired notice is dropped for the transcript line, an unpaired one stays. Stored notices are kept out of the turn-boundary pass so they cannot re-window assistant matching, and out of the first-user-row check that gates auto-title. Every client already renders a history user row through the synthetic split, and its live matcher (desktop reducer, phone store, Android ThreadStoreReducer) already treats history rows as transcript rows, so a replay after a reload or re-seed lands on the stored row. The id prefix is not the live row's task_ prefix, which the desktop reducer skips.

notExercised: No schema change: the rows use the existing messages table, so nothing migrates. Notices from before this release were never stored and still show only if the transcript has their line.
No live Claude session was run with a notice the CLI dropped; the tests build the stored row the way the registry writes it.

A task notified twice keeps only its first stored notice (INSERT OR IGNORE), and a task that notified before this release and again later, with the later line dropped, pairs its stored notice with the older line.
Older clients need no change: the stored row reaches them as an ordinary history user row, which they already split into the compact row.
